deepseek-v4-flash._variants_note: ⛔ 'max' REMOVED 2026-09-04, and 'medium' with it because opencode never declared it. DIAGNOSED FROM opencode.db, not guessed: under --variant max this model reasons until it hits a 32,000-token OUTPUT ceiling and returns a message whose parts are {step-start, reasoning, step-finish} with NO text part -- so opencode prints nothing to stdout and exits 0, and era sees a clean exit with an empty capture. Two messages in the local opencode.db have output=32000 EXACTLY, and BOTH have 0 text chars; a SUCCESSFUL run on the same bundle came in at 31,942 output tokens, 58 short of failing. deepseek folds reasoning into the output count (its 'reasoning' field reads 0 while output is tens of thousands, unlike muse-spark which reports ~11k separately), so maximum effort can spend the entire ceiling before a single answer token is written. This model's useful answers are ~3k tokens. ⚠ THE BENEFIT IS UNPROVEN. The single validation run at 'high' was INCONCLUSIVE -- era's own stall detector tree-killed it at 620.94s of no output growth while the model was still generating (opencode.db shows that turn as completed=NO, output=0), so it says nothing about whether 'high' avoids the ceiling. What survives is the correlation above, not a demonstrated cure: this is a reasonable change on token-accounting evidence, and it should not be described as a fix until a run at 'high' is observed finishing on its own. 'high' IS declared by opencode for this model, and costs nothing in stall budget on any real bundle: the bundle-size overlay dominates the variant base above ~30k tokens (measured 620.94s either way at 124,188 bytes; only a tiny bundle moves, 570s -> 300s, still generous).

muse-spark-1.2-contributor.note: ⭐ SAME RULE AS ox-alpha-free BELOW: the `variants` list is what sets the stall threshold, and without an entry here era resolves variant='default' (120s stall base) and kills a reasoning model mid-think having captured only its banner. muse-spark is reasoning-capable with a 1,048,576-token context, so it will absolutely think longer than 120s on a real bundle. `--variant max` verified accepted 2026-08-26 by running `opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.2-contributor --variant max` directly, which printed its `> build · muse-spark-1.2-contributor` banner and then the expected answer. Added at the same time as the preset, because a preset without this entry is a reviewer that cannot review. THE `--variant max` VERIFICATION ABOVE IS LEFT STANDING AS THE RECORD AND IS WORTHLESS AS EVIDENCE: acceptance proves nothing, because opencode does not validate variant names at all (`--variant totally-bogus-zzz` is accepted too, measured 2026-09-04). This model declares minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh and has no 'max', so what that check confirmed was a no-op. Corrected to `xhigh` on 2026-09-04. SUPERSEDED in the default panel by 1.3 on 2026-09-04, and KEPT rather than deleted: 1.2 is still active, `-Model` is used verbatim by the adapter, and without this entry an explicit pin to 1.2 would fall back to variant='default' and its 120s stall base.

muse-spark-1.3-contributor.note: ⭐ SAME RULE AS 1.2 ABOVE AND ox-alpha-free BELOW: the `variants` list is what sets era's OWN stall threshold, and without an entry here era resolves variant='default' (120s stall base) and kills a reasoning model mid-think having captured only its banner. Added 2026-09-04 with the 1.2 -> 1.3 default bump. `--variant max` verified accepted that day by running `opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor --variant max` directly. Also verified the same day: era does NOT pass `--variant default` -- backends/opencode.ps1 omits the flag entirely when the resolved variant is 'default' -- so this list is the only thing that makes the flag appear at all. (`--variant default` IS accepted by opencode if passed; era simply does not pass it.) ✅ RESOLVED THE SAME DAY, AND THE VALUE ABOVE CHANGED AS A RESULT. This entry said `max` for one commit, copied from 1.2. `opencode models --verbose` declares this model's variants as minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh -- THERE IS NO `max`. And OPENCODE DOES NOT VALIDATE VARIANT NAMES: measured, `--variant totally-bogus-zzz` returns exit 0 and a normal answer, identical in shape to `--variant max`. So the undeclared name was being silently IGNORED and this seat ran at opencode's DEFAULT reasoning effort while era believed it had asked for maximum -- from 2026-08-26, when muse-spark entered the default panel, to 2026-09-04. Now `xhigh`, which the model actually declares. THE REGISTRY HALF COULD NOT BE CHANGED ALONE: era's preference loop is @('xhigh','max','high','medium','low') and had to learn 'xhigh' in the same commit, or it would match nothing here, fall back to variant='default', and hand a reasoning model the 120s stall base -- turning a silent no-op into the ox-alpha kill. Resolve-OpencodeStallPlan gives 'xhigh' and 'max' the same 600s budget on purpose: they are two providers' names for "think as long as you like", not two tiers. Guarded by tests/OpencodeVariantDeclared.Tests.ps1 against tests/fixtures/opencode-declared-variants.json, a dated snapshot of what opencode declares.

ox-alpha-free.note: ⭐ THE `variants` LIST IS WHAT SETS THE STALL THRESHOLD, AND WITHOUT IT THIS MODEL CANNOT BE REVIEWED WITH. Measured 2026-08-22: ox-alpha prints its `> build · ox-alpha-free` banner (38 bytes) and then thinks SILENTLY for minutes — observed real review runs of 1m20s and 7m41s. With no map entry era resolves variant='default', whose stall base is 120s, so it was killed at 130s wall having emitted only the banner. Two smoke tests failed that way before the cause was found. `--variant max` is accepted by the model (verified directly) and raises the stall base to 600s. ⛔ The model itself was never the problem: `opencode run` direct answers in 20-23s, both with and without `-f` attach.

ox-alpha.notes: ⛔ RETIRED 2026-08-26 — OPENCODE NO LONGER OFFERS THIS MODEL. `opencode models` does not list ox-alpha at all any more, so every dispatch to it returns nothing. Observed the same day on a live panel: rounds 1-3 each produced an ox-alpha response, and it was absent from `opencode models` by the afternoon. (An earlier version of this note claimed round 4 dispatched it and got nothing, i.e. a silent 4 -> 3 degradation. That was WRONG and is retracted: round 4 was invoked with an explicit 3-reviewer -Reviewer list, so ox-alpha was never asked. The withdrawal is established from `opencode models`; no degradation event was observed) — the exact failure the note below was added to protect against, arriving from the other direction. Replaced in the default panel by `muse-spark`. Kept rather than deleted so the history stays legible and an explicit `-Reviewer ox-alpha` still resolves and fails loudly instead of resolving to nothing. ORIGINAL NOTE: opencode run -m opencode-go/ox-alpha-free. models.dev display name 'Ox Alpha Free (Unlimited)'. FREE tier, so it carries no cost ceiling and is safe to add to the default panel. Model id confirmed 2026-08-22 from `opencode models`. Added to the default panel the same day, taking it 3 -> 4 reviewers, after a round in which deepseek-flash ERRORED and the panel silently degraded to 2 (reference_era_tooling_defects_2026_08_09): a 4th free reviewer buys redundancy against exactly that.

muse-spark.notes: opencode run -m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor. models.dev display name is exactly 'Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor'. BUMPED 1.2 -> 1.3 on 2026-09-04 at the operator's request. Verified that day from `opencode models --verbose`: status active, 1,048,576 context / 131,072 max output, cost $0.10/$0.20 per Mtok (cache read $0.002) -- IDENTICAL to 1.2 on every one of those, so the swap is not a cost or ceiling change. release_date 2026-09-02. era sends `--variant xhigh` for this model. It sent `--variant max` for one commit, copied from 1.2, and that was wrong: opencode declares minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh here and no 'max'. Acceptance is not evidence -- opencode does not validate variant names, so `--variant totally-bogus-zzz` is accepted too (measured 2026-09-04) -- so the undeclared name was silently ignored and the seat ran at DEFAULT reasoning effort. The map entry stays load-bearing for a second reason: it is what keeps era's stall base at 600s instead of the 120s that kills a reasoning model mid-think (the ox-alpha failure). 1.2 IS STILL ACTIVE and its map entry is deliberately kept, so `-Model opencode-go/muse-spark-1.2-contributor` still gets variant=max rather than a 120s stall. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: a bare hint of `muse` now matches BOTH and the resolver warns and takes the lexically first model id, which is 1.2 -- name the version if you mean 1.3. NOTE the seat is NOT free, unlike ox-alpha whose whole justification for the 4th seat was zero marginal cost -- but at ~$0.01 per 100k-token round it is cheaper than deepseek-flash and immaterial next to opus. There is also an `opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` on the zen v1 endpoint; it is a DIFFERENT model and not the one named.
